# Components Catalog

<!-- Generated by `make catalog` (scripts/controls-catalog.mjs) from the Storybook stories. Don't edit by hand. -->

195 controls in 26 sections, one per Storybook Docs page. Each description is the one shown at the top of that page; each name links to the page in the [latest release's Storybook](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/).

## 3D

**[ModelViewer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/3d-modelviewer--docs)**: A 3D model viewer (three.js) for glTF, STL and OBJ files, with view presets, orbit or turntable controls, grid, axes, wireframe and measurement. The canvas has a text description (title, dimensions and triangle count), and every control is a button.

## Actions

**[ActionBar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/actions-actionbar--docs)**: A floating bar for acting on the selected items of a table, list or grid: "3 selected", a button that clears the selection, and the actions. Controlled by the app: pass the selection's size and a way to clear it, and handle the actions with `onAction` (or each item's own `onAction`). When the selection empties while focus is in the bar, focus goes back to where it was when the bar appeared, such as the row checkbox; if that's gone (deleted with the selection), to the first control left in the list around it.

**[Button](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/actions-button--docs)**: Buttons perform actions; with `href` they navigate. Built on React Aria's Button and Link, so press, keyboard and focus behaviour work the same on mouse, touch and keyboard.

**[ButtonGroup](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/actions-buttongroup--docs)**: Lays out a row of buttons, for example a dialog or form footer. In narrow containers (under 24rem) the buttons stack full width, with the last one (usually the primary action) on top.

**[IconButton](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/actions-iconbutton--docs)**: A button that shows only an icon. Its `aria-label` is required by its type.

**[Pagination](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/actions-pagination--docs)**: Previous and next buttons with the range shown ("1–25 of 1,203"), for anything paged: offset paging adds page numbers that collapse with an ellipsis, and an optional page-size choice; cursor paging shows only previous and next. A `nav` landmark, with `aria-current="page"` on the current page. DataTable's pager is built on it.

**[ToggleButton](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/actions-togglebutton--docs)**: A button that stays pressed until pressed again, for a setting that's on or off: bold, mute, a filter. Alone it's a toggle button (`aria-pressed`), controlled with `isSelected` / `onChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultSelected`. In a ToggleButtonGroup give it an `id`; the group holds the selection.

**[Toolbar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/actions-toolbar--docs)**: Controls that share one Tab stop: the arrow keys move between them (following `orientation`, reversed right to left), Tab leaves the toolbar, and coming back returns to the control used last. Put buttons, ToggleButtons, ToggleButtonGroups and Separators in `children`. `items` adds actions with priority-based overflow: when they don't all fit, the lowest-priority ones move into a "More actions" menu at the end, which runs the same actions. Nothing moves while everything fits.

## Canvas

**[Canvas](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/canvas-canvas--docs)**: A pannable, zoomable world with a grid, snapping, marquee selection, rulers, a minimap and zoom controls.

## Chart

**[Box Plot](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-box-plot--docs)**: Nightly seeing at four sites in summer and winter, from raw values: boxes from the lower to the upper quartile with the median across, whiskers to the furthest nights within 1.5 times the box, the mean as a diamond, and bad nights as hollow dots. The table gives the five numbers.

**[Bullet](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-bullet--docs)**: A measure against a target over qualitative ranges: a `meter` whose text gives the value, the target and the range the value is in.

**[Candlestick](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-candlestick--docs)**: A year of daily candles for the fictional STAR index, with volume in a pane below and a 50-day average. Up candles are hollow, down candles filled. Hover or touch the plot for the crosshair: the readout above shows that day's open, high, low, close, change and volume. Pinch, Ctrl+wheel or drag to zoom; Reset zoom returns.

**[Charts](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-charts--docs)**: Usage (area, with a dashed forecast), solar (bars) and temperature (on a right axis), in Denver time, with a contract limit and a normal band. Hover or tap for every series at that time; click the legend to hide or highlight; drag across the chart to select a range (pinch and pan on touch).

**[Events](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-events--docs)**: Five deploys on a 7-day latency chart: a dashed line and a marker chip on the time axis for each. The third and fourth, an hour apart, cluster into one chip ("2 events"). Every chip is a button (Tab to it); pressing one opens its detail. The events are also in the summary and in "View as table".

**[Funnel](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-funnel--docs)**: Observing proposals from submission to observation: each step's bar is as wide as its count, labelled with its share of the first step. The summary gives the overall share and the largest drop; the table adds each step's share of the one before.

**[Heatmap](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-heatmap--docs)**: Topics by weeks on a sequential scale, with values in the cells and weeks not yet practised hatched.

**[Latency](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-latency--docs)**: 24 hours of observatory network latency: p50, p95 and p99 lines with the space between them shaded, and a p95 objective of 300 ms. The two windows where p95 went over it are shaded, marked on the time axis (Tab to them) and described in the summary; "View as table" lists every percentile.

**[Live](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-live--docs)**: Tracking error for three telescope domes at 10 points a second, over a 5-minute window, started from history (a still frame: nothing streams). Hover or touch the plot to pause it; the Pause button does the same.

**[Outcomes](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-outcomes--docs)**: Four outcomes over 90 days as lines, on a 0–100% axis, with three news events and the latest values in the legend.

**[Radar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-radar--docs)**: Two instruments scored from 0 to 5 on six measures: each series is a filled shape with its own colour and point shape. The legend shows, hides and highlights series; the summary names each one's best and worst measure.

**[Sankey](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-sankey--docs)**: The observatory's energy for a year, from its sources through the switchboard to its uses: each band is as wide as its flow, coloured by where it goes (`linkColor="target"`). Hover or tap a band or node to highlight its flows; the table lists every flow with its share of its source.

**[Scatter](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-scatter--docs)**: Candidate telescope sites: altitude against clear nights a year, in two series with their own colours and point shapes. The tooltip names each site; the summary gives each series' ranges and how strongly the two move together; the table lists every point. Drag (with a mouse) or pinch to zoom.

**[Treemap](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-treemap--docs)**: Storage use by instrument at three sites (40 instruments), coloured by the change on last month: green for growth, red for shrinking. Press a site's header (or Enter on it) to drill in, and the breadcrumbs (or Backspace) to come back. Arrow keys move between rectangles, each named with its value and share.

**[Waterfall](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chart-waterfall--docs)**: An observatory's budget bridge from September to October: increases in green and decreases in red, each labelled with its sign, totals in neutral, and dashed connectors at the running total. On a phone the steps run down the page. The summary names the start, the end and the largest increase and decrease; the table lists running totals.

## Chat

**[Composer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chat-composer--docs)**: The message box of a chat, with mentions, commands, attachments and emoji.

**[EmojiPicker](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chat-emojipicker--docs)**: A searchable emoji grid by category, with recent emoji, a skin-tone choice and a preview of the focused emoji's CLDR name. Each emoji is a button named by its CLDR name ("thumbs up").

**[MessageList](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chat-messagelist--docs)**: A chat transcript: bottom-anchored and virtualised, grouped by author with day separators, an unread divider, "Jump to latest", reactions, replies, delivery status and per-message actions. String bodies render as Markdown.

**[ReactionBar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/chat-reactionbar--docs)**: Reactions as toggle chips (`aria-pressed`) with counts, who reacted, and a button to add one.

## Codes

**[Barcode](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/codes-barcode--docs)**: A linear barcode with an accessible name, drawn as SVG or canvas.

**[QRCode](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/codes-qrcode--docs)**: A QR code with an accessible name, drawn as SVG or canvas.

## Dashboard

**[Dashboard](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/dashboard-dashboard--docs)**: The least a host writes: a dashboard from a literal, widgets with only a type, a size and a source (PERS-06).

**[DashboardGrid](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/dashboard-dashboardgrid--docs)**: Panels on the default 12-column grid. Phones stack them; tablets halve the columns.

**[DashboardWidget](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/dashboard-dashboardwidget--docs)**: A widget on its own (DATA-18), fed by a bare `load` function: the same frame, states and data loading.

**[ManageDashboardsDialog](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/dashboard-managedashboardsdialog--docs)**: Rename, reorder (drag or buttons), move pages between dashboards, copy, delete, then Apply once (§13).

**[PageSettingsDialog](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/dashboard-pagesettingsdialog--docs)**: Title, columns, row sizing, density and compaction, with a preview of the rescaled layout (EDIT-26, GRID-03).

**[WidgetFrame](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/dashboard-widgetframe--docs)**: The chrome around a dashboard widget: a labelled region with its title, a single action menu (refresh, configure, expand and the edit actions, plus the widget type's and the host's), a subtle refreshing indicator, and in edit mode its lock and setup status. The body takes the rest of the frame.

## DICOM

**[DicomViewer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/dicom-dicomviewer--docs)**: A review viewer for DICOM image stacks with stack scrolling, window and level, zoom and pan, measurements, overlay text, series thumbnails and full screen. Every tool works from the keyboard, and the slice position, window and measurements are exposed as text. Not for diagnostic use.

## Diff

**[DiffViewer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/diff-diffviewer--docs)**: A line diff with word highlights, collapsed context, hunk navigation, and split or unified layout.

**[PlanReview](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/diff-planreview--docs)**: Reviews a plan of resource changes: summary, filters, a structural diff per change, and a confirmed Apply.

## Display

**[ActivityTimeline](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-activitytimeline--docs)**: A history of events (audit logs, deploys, account history, incidents): a vertical rail of icons or avatars, each event as "actor action target" with a relative timestamp (the exact time on hover or focus) and detail that expands inline. Grouped under day headings in the given time zone; older items load from a "Load more" button or when the end scrolls into view.

**[AnchorNav](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-anchornav--docs)**: An "on this page" table of contents in a `nav` landmark. Its links come from `items`, or from the headings in `contentRef` (such as a Markdown document). As the page, or `scrollRef`, scrolls, the section being read is marked `aria-current="location"`. Choosing a link scrolls its section to the top (smoothly, unless the user prefers reduced motion), clear of `scrollOffset`, moves focus to it, and with `shouldUpdateHash` puts it in the URL. Vertical, it's a sticky sidebar with nested levels; horizontal, a bar of jump links. On phones both become a menu button showing the current section.

**[Avatar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-avatar--docs)**: A person's picture, or their initials on a colour picked from their name, with an optional presence dot. An `img` named by the name (and presence).

**[Badge](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-badge--docs)**: A short, non-interactive label: a count, a status or a category.

**[Breadcrumbs](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-breadcrumbs--docs)**: The trail of pages leading to the current one, in a `nav` landmark. Every item with an `href` is a link through `UIProvider`'s `LinkComponent`; the last item is the current page (`aria-current="page"`). When the trail doesn't fit, the middle items collapse into a menu (whose items are links too), keeping the first item and as many of the items nearest the current page as fit.

**[Card](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-card--docs)**: A surface that groups related content, with an optional header (title, icon, actions) and footer.

**[Carousel](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-carousel--docs)**: Slides of any content with previous and next buttons, dots or thumbnails, swipes, mouse drags and the arrow keys, following the WAI-ARIA carousel pattern. Shows one slide or several at once (by its own width), moves a slide or a page at a time, and can loop. Slides out of view are inert and hidden from assistive technology; a polite live region reads the new slides as they come into view, except while autoplay runs. A carousel of its children: each child is a slide.

**[Chip](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-chip--docs)**: A compact label, such as an active filter, optionally removable with its own button.

**[CodeBlock](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-codeblock--docs)**: Code with syntax colours, copy and wrap, line numbers and highlighted lines, scrolling inside itself.

**[DescriptionList](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-descriptionlist--docs)**: Label/value rows, such as a record's details. Rows flow into columns that adapt to the container: one on phones, more on wider screens. Secondary rows hide behind "Show more".

**[Disclosure](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-disclosure--docs)**: A section that expands and collapses. The trigger is a real button with `aria-expanded`, inside a heading. Controlled with `isExpanded` / `onExpandedChange` or uncontrolled with `defaultExpanded`.

**[EventCalendar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-eventcalendar--docs)**: Events on a calendar: a month grid (events in day cells, bars across days, "+N more" for the rest), week and day time grids (hours down the side, overlapping events side by side, an all-day row and a line at the current time), and an agenda list. A view switch, previous / today / next and month and year Cyclers move around, reporting the visible range so the app can fetch its events. With `isEditable`, events move and resize by drag or with Alt and the arrow keys, snapping to `snapMinutes`, and dragging on empty time or days adds one; locked events stay put. Takes ScheduleTimeline's items and time zones, so the same events can show in both.

**[Flag](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-flag--docs)**: A country's flag from the registered countries (see FlagProvider), with any of its name, native name, code and languages beside it. An unknown country shows a generic flag icon.

**[GanttChart](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-ganttchart--docs)**: A Gantt chart: a task grid (a tree of summary tasks and tasks with their start, end, duration and progress) beside a timeline of bars, milestones and summary bars spanning their children, in a resizable split that shares rows and vertical scrolling. Dependencies of all four types are drawn as arrows; those the dates break are highlighted, and the critical path can be. The time scale zooms from hours to quarters, with a today line and shaded non-working time. With `isEditable`, bars move, resize and set progress by drag or with Alt and the arrow keys, snapping to `snapMinutes`, and dependencies are made by dragging from a bar's end or from a task's details. Rows are virtualized for thousands of tasks.

**[KanbanBoard](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-kanbanboard--docs)**: A board of columns holding cards, for tasks moving through statuses. Cards drag within and between columns (mouse, touch, keyboard and screen reader drag and drop) or move from their actions menu, and the app applies each move from `onMove`. Columns show their count against a work-in-progress limit and collapse; `lanes` splits the board into rows; chosen cards move together from an ActionBar. `isVirtualized` keeps boards of thousands of cards fast.

**[Kbd](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-kbd--docs)**: A keyboard key or shortcut, for example in a menu item or a hint.

**[Layout](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-layout--docs)**: Children in a column (or a row), evenly spaced. The default container for page and card content.

**[ListView](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-listview--docs)**: A list of rich rows: an icon or avatar, a label, a description, metadata and actions. Rows can be chosen (one or many, with checkboxes), activated (`onAction`), grouped under sticky headings (`sections`), dragged into order (`isReorderable`) and loaded page by page (`onLoadMore`). `isVirtualized` renders only the rows in view, for lists of thousands. It takes data and callbacks only.

**[LiveRegion](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-liveregion--docs)**: A visually hidden `aria-live` region.

**[Markdown](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-markdown--docs)**: Markdown as styled rich text, with no raw HTML.

**[Pillbox](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-pillbox--docs)**: A single choice from a few options, shown as joined buttons, for example a list/grid view switch. It's a radio group with the standard radio keyboard pattern: Tab reaches the chosen option and arrow keys choose the next or previous one. `onChange` receives the option's `id`, typed as the union of the ids in `options`.

**[PriceTicker](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-priceticker--docs)**: A live value with its change (▲/▼ and tone), a brief tint when it changes, an optional sparkline and a stale state. Not a live region unless `announceThreshold` is set.

**[Prose](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-prose--docs)**: Rich text (p, ul, ol, li, a, strong, em, code, pre, blockquote, h2–h4, table, hr) styled with the tokens.

**[RelativeTime](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-relativetime--docs)**: A relative time ("5 minutes ago") that keeps itself current from a shared clock (one timer for the whole page). The exact timestamp, in the given time zone, shows in a tooltip and is read by screen readers.

**[ScheduleTimeline](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-scheduletimeline--docs)**: A schedule of items on lanes (instruments, rooms, channels) over a day, a week or a custom number of days. Lanes are rows and time runs across, with a sticky lane column and time axis and a line at the current time. Items that overlap in a lane are stacked, hatched and marked. With `isEditable`, items move and resize by drag or with Alt and the arrow keys, snapping to `snapMinutes`, and dragging on empty space creates one. The lanes and items form a keyboard-navigable grid; narrow containers (phones) show an agenda grouped by lane and day instead.

**[ScrollRegion](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-scrollregion--docs)**: A focusable, labelled region that scrolls its content within `maxHeight`.

**[SecretReveal](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-secretreveal--docs)**: Credentials shown once, with reveal and copy per value.

**[SegmentedMeter](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-segmentedmeter--docs)**: A bar of stacked parts against a maximum, with limit markers, overflow hatching and a legend. It's a `meter` whose value text names every part.

**[Separator](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-separator--docs)**: A horizontal or vertical divider with `separator` semantics.

**[Sparkline](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-sparkline--docs)**: A small, wordless chart of a series, with a generated text summary for assistive technology.

**[SplitView](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-splitview--docs)**: Two or more resizable panes for master–detail lists, inspectors, editors with previews and log panes. Each handle is a focusable `separator`: drag it (mouse or touch), use the arrow keys (5% steps), Home and End, and Enter or a double-click to collapse and restore a collapsible neighbour. Sizes are reported for the app to keep. It adapts to its container's width: below `stackBelow` the last pane becomes a Drawer (or the panes stack).

**[StatTile](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-stattile--docs)**: A key figure with its label, unit, change and trend. Long values shrink to fit the tile's width.

**[StatusDot](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-statusdot--docs)**: A small status indicator: a coloured shape plus a text label.

**[Stepper](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-stepper--docs)**: Progress through an ordered set of steps, as a list (`ol`) with the current step marked `aria-current="step"`. Each step's status is in its marker, its colours and in words for screen readers. With `onCurrentStepChange`, steps are buttons that move to them (all of them, or with `isLinear` only those already reached) inside a `nav`. A horizontal stepper too narrow for its steps shows the compact variant; it fills its container's width. `hasProgressBar` and `hasStatusBadges` add an "N of M done" bar and each status in words, for a checklist.

**[Tabs](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-tabs--docs)**: Tabs switch between panels of related content. Controlled with `selectedKey` / `onSelectionChange` (for example to keep the tab in the URL) or uncontrolled with `defaultSelectedKey`. Arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs; `keyboardActivation="manual"` makes arrow keys move focus only, with Enter or Space selecting.

**[Text](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-text--docs)**: Body text in the app's type scale and token colours.

**[Tree](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-tree--docs)**: A Storybook-style sidebar: category headings, components with coloured icons and "new" badges, and their pages. Only pages are selectable (`selectableNodes="leaves"`): pressing a component opens it. Each row has a menu.

**[UptimeBar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-uptimebar--docs)**: Daily uptime as a row of thin bars coloured by threshold, with the overall uptime for the period and a summary ("99.95% over 90 days, 2 days below 99.9%"). Hover, focus or tap a day for its date, uptime and incidents. The days are a list of buttons with full names; arrow keys, Home and End move between them.

**[VisuallyHidden](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-visuallyhidden--docs)**: Content that's available to assistive technology but not shown on screen.

**[WorldClock](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/display-worldclock--docs)**: The current time in several time zones, digital or analog, from a list of IANA zones.

## Editor

**[RichTextEditor](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/editor-richtexteditor--docs)**: A WYSIWYG editor that stores Markdown, sanitised HTML or JSON.

## Feedback

**[Banner](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/feedback-banner--docs)**: The inline message component, for a page or inside a card or form.

**[EmptyState](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/feedback-emptystate--docs)**: Shown in place of content that has nothing to show yet.

**[ErrorState](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/feedback-errorstate--docs)**: Shown in place of content that failed to load. The message is announced (`role="alert"`) when it appears, the optional retry button shows its own pending state, and technical details stay out of the way in a disclosure.

**[ProgressBar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/feedback-progressbar--docs)**: Progress of a task: determinate (`value` between `minValue` and `maxValue`) or indeterminate.

**[RolloutProgress](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/feedback-rolloutprogress--docs)**: A staged rollout's progress: overall bar, elapsed time, controls, a stage stepper and the targets (filterable, grouped, failed first). Rollback goes through a confirmation; failures are announced, throttled.

**[Skeleton](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/feedback-skeleton--docs)**: A loading placeholder. Hidden from assistive technology: mark the loading region with `aria-busy` (and announce results when they arrive) instead.

**[Spinner](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/feedback-spinner--docs)**: An indeterminate loading indicator with an accessible label (a `progressbar` without a value).

**[Timer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/feedback-timer--docs)**: A countdown or count-up clock that doesn't drift, with warning and danger tones at its thresholds. It's a `timer` that doesn't announce every second; crossing a threshold and running out are announced.

**[Toast](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/feedback-toast--docs)**: Shows the toasts created with `toast()`. UIProvider renders one, so apps normally don't. Hovering or focusing it pauses every countdown. Stays usable while a modal dialog is open.

## Finance

**[DepthChart](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/finance-depthchart--docs)**: A depth chart: cumulative size by price, a step area per side (bids to the left of the mid price, asks to the right), labelled on the plot. It has a title, a generated summary for screen readers, and "View as table".

**[OrderBook](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/finance-orderbook--docs)**: An order book: asks above, bids below, and the spread and mid price between them, with size bars, a price grouping Select, and pressable levels. Changed sizes flash and show ▲/▼ for a moment. Built for live feeds: props can change many times a second and the table renders at most once per animation frame. "Read best prices" announces the best bid, best ask and spread on request.

**[ProbabilityBar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/finance-probabilitybar--docs)**: A YES/NO split bar with both percentages labelled ("Yes 62%", "No 38%"). The percentages are whole numbers that add up to 100.

**[TradeTicket](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/finance-tradeticket--docs)**: An order ticket for exchanges and binary (YES/NO) markets: toned side choice, market or limit, an amount or a quantity, the app's estimate (average price, quantity, cost, fees, payout and return, slippage), the balance and the app's warnings. Review opens a confirmation summarising the order; confirming awaits `onSubmit`. Works by keyboard alone: arrow keys choose within the radio groups and Tab moves between them and the fields.

## Form

**[ConfigForm](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/form-configform--docs)**: A form described as data. It renders the fields from the config (through the field registry), owns the values (with TanStack Form), validates them (on blur first, then on change, everything on submit), and runs the submit lifecycle: server field and form errors, a needs-confirmation step, and focus on the first invalid field. Parents observe through callbacks; they never hold a second copy of the values. `mode="view"` shows the same config as a read-only description list.

**[Containers](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/form-containers--docs)**: DialogForm: the buttons sit in the dialog footer. It can't be dismissed while saving; with unsaved changes Escape and the backdrop don't close it, and Cancel asks first. Full screen on phones.

**[Sample CRUD](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/form-sample-crud--docs)**: A small CRUD screen built from one tariff config: create and edit in dialogs (with Delete), a guided wizard, and a pretend server that rejects duplicate names (a field error from problem+json), reports a conflict (a form error) and asks to confirm rates above $1. The region list follows the country and resets with it; the rate fields follow the pricing type.

## Foundations

**[Colour tokens](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/foundations-colour-tokens--docs)**: _No description yet._

## Graph

**[NodeGraph](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/graph-nodegraph--docs)**: A node-and-edge diagram with automatic layout, status, selection, keyboard navigation and optional editing.

**[OrgChart](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/graph-orgchart--docs)**: An organisation as a tidy tree of people, with expand and collapse, search, pan and zoom.

## Inputs

**[Calendar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-calendar--docs)**: A calendar on the page, without a field: pick one date, several (`selectionMode="multiple"`), or browse by week (`view="week"`). Its header has month and year Cyclers to jump straight to any month or year (`headerControls`). Shows several months side by side with `visibleMonths`, and dots, badges, prices and highlights on days with `getDayInfo`. Supports `minValue`/`maxValue`, `isDateUnavailable` and `firstDayOfWeek`. Give it an `aria-label` saying what the date is for.

**[Checkbox](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-checkbox--docs)**: A single checkbox with its label, on its own (`isSelected` / `onChange`) or as an option in a `CheckboxGroup` (`value`). `isIndeterminate` shows a dash for a partly selected parent. The whole label row is the touch target.

**[CheckboxGroup](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-checkboxgroup--docs)**: Several related checkboxes with one label, description and error, for example notification channels. The value is the array of checked options' `value`s.

**[CidrField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-cidrfield--docs)**: An IPv4 or IPv6 CIDR block input that normalises, validates and shows the range.

**[ColorField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-colorfield--docs)**: A colour choice: swatches from the chart palette (which follow the theme), plus a custom colour. The value is the palette slot (`chart-3`), so charts recolour with the theme, or a hex string for a custom colour.

**[ComboBox](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-combobox--docs)**: A text input with a list of suggestions: typeahead over static `items`, or async results from `loadItems`. Value is the chosen option's `id` (`value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange`); with `allowsCustomValue` the typed text can stand on its own (`inputValue` / `onInputChange`).

**[CopyField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-copyfield--docs)**: A read-only value with a copy button.

**[Cycler](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-cycler--docs)**: Arrows step (hold one to keep going) and wrap from December to January. Press the month to jump to any.

**[DatePicker](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-datepicker--docs)**: A date input (`CalendarDate`): type into the month, day and year segments, or pick from a calendar that opens in a popover (a full-screen sheet on phones). Supports `minValue`/`maxValue`, `isDateUnavailable` and `firstDayOfWeek`.

**[DateRangePicker](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-daterangepicker--docs)**: A date range input: start and end segments, or a range calendar in a popover (a full-screen sheet on phones) where the first press picks one end and the second press the other. Supports `minValue`/`maxValue`, `maxRangeDays` and `isDateUnavailable`.

**[DateTimePicker](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-datetimepicker--docs)**: A date and time input (`ZonedDateTime`) in a time zone (`timeZone`, or the provider's default). Type into the segments, or pick a day from the calendar and set the time below it, in a popover (a full-screen sheet with large time entry on phones). 12- or 24-hour display comes from the locale unless `hourCycle` is set.

**[DropZone](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-dropzone--docs)**: A target for dragging and dropping files, built on React Aria's DropZone: it highlights while files are dragged over it, and keyboard and screen reader users can focus it and paste files. It does no checking or uploading; `FileField` adds a file chooser, validation, a file list and uploads.

**[FileField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-filefield--docs)**: Choose files with a button, or drag and drop or paste them onto the drop zone. Files are checked against `accept`, `maxSize` and `maxFiles`, and listed with their size, upload progress and errors, each with a remove button. With an `upload` function the field uploads each file as it's added; otherwise the app reports progress and errors by updating the items (controlled `value`).

**[FlagPicker](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-flagpicker--docs)**: Choose a country from flag thumbnails in titled rows that wrap to the panel's width, with a search. The value is the country's code; `onChange` also receives the country's registered data (names, languages and the app's own fields).

**[IconPicker](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-iconpicker--docs)**: Choose an icon from a set the app supplies: a searchable grid (arrow keys move in two dimensions) in a popover. The value is the icon's `id`.

**[InlineEdit](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-inlineedit--docs)**: _No description yet._

**[JsonEditor](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-jsoneditor--docs)**: A JSON document in a field: monospaced, growing, checked as you type, with a Format button.

**[KeyValueEditor](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-keyvalueeditor--docs)**: An editor for key/value pairs with paste-to-split, duplicate checks, reordering and secret values.

**[Knob](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-knob--docs)**: A rotary knob: a `slider` whose value shows as an arc. Drag up or down to turn it (Shift for fine), use the wheel while it's focused, or the arrow keys (PageUp/PageDown take 10 steps); double-click or press Enter to reset, or type a value in the field under it. `isBipolar` fills from the centre with a detent there, `scale="log"` suits frequencies, and `unit` is shown and announced with the value.

**[MarkdownEditor](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-markdowneditor--docs)**: A Markdown source editor with a formatting toolbar and a live preview.

**[MaskedField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-maskedfield--docs)**: A text input with a pattern mask: phone numbers, postal codes, card numbers, dates, IBANs. The mask's literals appear as the user types and the caret skips over them; pasted text with or without them fills the slots. The value is the raw characters by default (`valueFormat` for the formatted text), `onComplete` fires when the mask is full, the keyboard follows the mask (numeric for digits), and an incomplete value is invalid on submit.

**[MoneyField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-moneyfield--docs)**: An amount of money as a decimal string, so it never drifts the way floats do. Formats for the locale when not focused, shows plain digits for editing, and accepts pasted amounts with symbols and grouping. Screen readers hear the amount with the currency's name ("1,234.50 US dollars"). Combine amounts with the decimal helpers (`decimalAdd`, `decimalMultiply`, `roundHalfEven`…).

**[MultiSelect](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-multiselect--docs)**: Choose several options; the chosen values show as removable chips and drop out of the suggestions. Static `items` are filtered as you type, or `loadItems` fetches results. Backspace in the empty input removes the last chip. Built on React Aria's single-selection combo box: each pick adds a chip and clears the query.

**[NumberField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-numberfield--docs)**: A number input that parses and formats for the locale (`UIProvider`'s `locale`): "1.234,5" in German, currency with the currency's own fraction digits through `formatOptions`, percentages, units. Typing, pasting and IME input are never filtered keystroke by keystroke; the text is parsed when committed. ArrowUp/ArrowDown step by `step`, PageUp/PageDown by a larger amount, and Home/End jump to `minValue`/`maxValue`.

**[OneTimeCodeField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-onetimecodefield--docs)**: A one-time code (verification code, PIN) in cells: one input underneath, so it's one field to screen readers and to autofill (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`, a numeric keyboard for digits). Pasting or autofilling a whole code fills every cell; Backspace and the arrow keys move between cells; typing over a filled cell replaces it. `groupSizes` splits the cells (3 + 3), `isMasked` hides the characters, and `onComplete` fires when every cell is filled.

**[PropertyInspector](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-propertyinspector--docs)**: Edits the selected object's (or objects') properties, in collapsible groups, with scrubbable numbers.

**[RadioGroup](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-radiogroup--docs)**: A single choice from a short list of options, all visible at once. Arrow keys move the choice between options and Tab leaves the group in one step. The value type is inferred from `value` or `onChange`, so a group bound to a union-typed state gets that union back.

**[RangeSlider](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-rangeslider--docs)**: A range on a scale, with a thumb for each end; the thumbs can't cross. Takes the same props as `Slider`, with `[start, end]` values.

**[Rating](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-rating--docs)**: A star rating input: a slider whose arrow keys step, and where a pointer takes the icon (or half icon with `step={0.5}`) under it, with a hover preview. `isClearable` lets choosing the current value again clear it, and `isReadOnly` keeps it focusable but unchangeable. `icon`, `size` and `tone` change the look. To show a rating in a table or list, use RatingDisplay.

**[ReorderableList](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-reorderablelist--docs)**: Items to put in order by dragging or with move buttons, each move announced.

**[RuleBuilder](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-rulebuilder--docs)**: Builds a rule from conditions in AND/OR groups and the actions to run when it matches, with a summary.

**[RuleList](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-rulelist--docs)**: Rules in order, first match wins, with drag-to-reorder and an on/off switch per rule.

**[ScheduleEditor](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-scheduleeditor--docs)**: A full-day schedule of power limits in kW, with the 24-hour preview.

**[SearchField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-searchfield--docs)**: A search input with a clear button. Escape clears it (and, when already empty, passes through, for example to close a dialog). `onChange` reports every keystroke; `onSearch` is debounced for live results.

**[Select](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-select--docs)**: Choose one option from a list. Value is the chosen option's `id` (`value` / `defaultValue` / `onChange`). Keyboard: arrows, typeahead, Enter, Escape. On phones the list opens as a bottom sheet.

**[Slider](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-slider--docs)**: A value on a scale from `minValue` to `maxValue` (0–100 by default). Set `step` for discrete values, `ticks` for labelled marks and `formatOptions` (`Intl.NumberFormat`) for the value shown and announced. Arrow keys step, PageUp/PageDown take bigger steps, Home/End jump to the ends; the track can be clicked, tapped or dragged. `orientation="vertical"` makes a fader.

**[SlugField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-slugfield--docs)**: A URL slug input derived from a source text, with optional async validation.

**[Switch](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-switch--docs)**: An on/off setting that takes effect immediately, such as "Email notifications". It's a checkbox with `role="switch"`: Space toggles it, and the whole label row is the touch target.

**[TagField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-tagfield--docs)**: Free-text values as tags, in the standard field frame. Enter or a delimiter adds the typed text, and pasted lists split into tags. Backspace in the empty input takes the last tag into the input to edit (Enter on a tag edits that one; Delete removes it): Enter or leaving the field puts it back in place, and Escape cancels. Repeats and tags past `maxItems` are refused with a message; `validateTag` marks invalid tags. Optional `suggestions` filter as you type, and `isReorderable` lets tags be dragged into order.

**[TemplateEditor](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-templateeditor--docs)**: An SMS template with keyword suggestions, a live example, an SMS counter and a keyword list.

**[TextArea](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-textarea--docs)**: Multi-line text in the standard field frame. It grows with its content between `minRows` and `maxRows`.

**[TextField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-textfield--docs)**: A single-line text input in the standard field frame.

**[TierEditor](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-tiereditor--docs)**: Price per kWh by monthly usage; the last tier is open-ended. Adding a tier starts at the last one's end.

**[TileGrid](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-tilegrid--docs)**: Tiles in titled rows that wrap to the available width, with two-dimensional keyboard navigation.

**[TilePicker](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-tilepicker--docs)**: The base of IconPicker and FlagPicker: rows with titles, tiles the app draws, and a search. Arrow keys move across rows; `onChange` receives the option with its `data`.

**[TimeField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-timefield--docs)**: A time input: hour, minute (and optionally second) segments, typed or stepped with the arrow keys. The value type follows `value`, `defaultValue` or `placeholderValue` (`Time`, `CalendarDateTime` or `ZonedDateTime`). 12- or 24-hour display comes from the locale unless `hourCycle` is set; `granularity` picks the smallest unit and `hideTimeZone` hides a zoned value's zone.

**[TimeRangePicker](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-timerangepicker--docs)**: Picks a time range for dashboards and charts: presets (configurable), a relative range ("last 3 hours") or an absolute range between two date-times. The value is a plain object (`TimeRange`) that apps can keep in the URL and turn into instants with `resolveTimeRange`. The trigger shows the range's label; the choices open in a popover, or a full-screen sheet with the presets first on phones. Presets apply at once; the other entries apply with Apply.

**[TransferList](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-transferlist--docs)**: Two lists, available and chosen, with buttons to move the selected rows or every shown row either way, a search field and select-all over each, and drag and drop between them. The value is the chosen ids, in order; `isReorderable` lets users drag them into order. Both lists render only the rows in view, so thousands of items stay fast.

**[UnitField](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/inputs-unitfield--docs)**: A duration in milliseconds, typed as friendly units: a number with a unit Select, or text such as "90s", "2h" or "1h30m". Shows the value in the largest units that keep it whole once committed, and announces it in words ("1 hour 30 minutes"). Min and max are in milliseconds, with errors in friendly units.

## Logs

**[LogViewer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/logs-logviewer--docs)**: A virtualised log viewer for streams of 100k+ lines. It follows the newest line until scrolled up, then offers "Jump to latest (N new)". Search takes text or a `/regex/`, with highlighted matches and next/previous; the level filter, wrap, error announcements and a .log download sit in the toolbar. The log is a `log` region with `aria-live="off"`, so lines aren't read out unless "Announce errors" is on.

## Map

**[Choropleth](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/map-choropleth--docs)**: Requests per second by region on a 5-step scale, with a legend, a summary naming the highest and lowest, and the regions listed by value below (focus one to highlight it on the map). Hover or tap a region for its tooltip. Markers sit on top. The regions are a synthetic grid, so the story works offline.

**[Map](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/map-map--docs)**: Sites as markers, coloured and shaped by status. Nearby markers cluster (press a cluster to zoom in); the selected site shows a card. Every marker is in the list below the map too. This story's style has no tiles, so it works offline; apps pass their own style URL.

## Math

**[CoordinatePlane](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/math-coordinateplane--docs)**: A plane with functions, points, segments, vectors and polygons, which pans, zooms and reads values.

**[Markdown](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/math-markdown--docs)**: Markdown as styled rich text, with no raw HTML.

**[MathFormula](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/math-mathformula--docs)**: A TeX formula as MathML, inline or as a (numbered) block. Copying it copies the TeX.

**[MathInput](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/math-mathinput--docs)**: A formula field that edits TeX visually, with an optional palette of templates.

## Media

**[AudioMeter](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-audiometer--docs)**: Segmented level bars with peak hold, zones, latching clip indicators and a dB scale.

**[AudioPlayer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-audioplayer--docs)**: Plays audio with the shared transport, a waveform, a playlist and the system media controls.

**[FilePreview](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-filepreview--docs)**: A file's preview: a thumbnail card, the viewer itself, or a chip that opens the viewer, chosen by its MIME type.

**[ImageAnnotator](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-imageannotator--docs)**: Pins, rectangles and polygons on an image, in fractional coordinates so they survive resizing. Built on ImageViewer (zoom, pan and rotate still work): draw with the tools, drag to move, drag handles to resize, and edit the label and note in a popover. Every annotation is also in a side list that follows the selection and is fully keyboard editable; on the image, the arrow keys nudge the selected shape and Enter adds one in the middle of the view.

**[ImageGallery](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-imagegallery--docs)**: A responsive grid of square thumbnails, or a carousel of the images (`layout="carousel"`). Choosing one opens the Lightbox at that image; closing it returns focus to the image that opened it.

**[ImageViewer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-imageviewer--docs)**: Shows one image that can be zoomed (wheel, pinch, double-click or double-tap for 100%, + and −), panned (drag or arrow keys), rotated in quarter turns and reset (0). The image moves as a single transformed element, so even a very large photo zooms smoothly on a phone. Zoom changes are announced, and a broken image shows an ErrorState with its alt text.

**[Lightbox](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-lightbox--docs)**: A full-screen dialog for browsing images: each one can be zoomed, panned and rotated as in ImageViewer. Previous and next buttons, the arrow keys (when the image isn't panning), swipes and a strip of thumbnails change image, and the neighbouring images are preloaded. Focus is trapped inside and returns where it was on close.

**[MediaLibrary](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-medialibrary--docs)**: Stored files to browse, upload, describe, delete and pick from.

**[MediaTransport](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-mediatransport--docs)**: Play/pause, seek, time, skip, speed, volume and live controls, shared by every player.

**[PdfViewer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-pdfviewer--docs)**: Shows a PDF with on-demand pages, a text layer, search, zoom, thumbnails, download and print.

**[VideoPlayer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-videoplayer--docs)**: Plays progressive, HLS and DASH video with the shared transport, live controls, quality, captions and stats.

**[Waveform](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/media-waveform--docs)**: Peaks drawn as bars with a playhead; click, drag or use the arrows to seek.

## Music

**[MusicNotation](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/music-musicnotation--docs)**: A score rendered as music notation, with a playhead and a navigable text alternative.

**[MusicTransport](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/music-musictransport--docs)**: Play/pause, stop, position, tempo and loop controls for beat-based playback.

**[PianoKeyboard](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/music-pianokeyboard--docs)**: An on-screen piano keyboard with multi-touch, glissando, computer-keyboard and MIDI input.

**[PianoRoll](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/music-pianoroll--docs)**: A note editor with a keyboard, snapping grid, velocity lane and table view.

**[StepSequencer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/music-stepsequencer--docs)**: A drum-machine style grid of steps with velocities.

## Overlays

**[CommandPalette](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-commandpalette--docs)**: A command palette: press ⌘K / Ctrl+K (or a `CommandPaletteTrigger`) to open a search over the app's pages and actions. Matching is fuzzy over labels and keywords, with matched letters highlighted; recent items come first before a query, and `loadItems` adds async results (records, resources) under their own sections. Arrow keys move, Enter runs (an item's `onAction`, or its `href` through the app's router), Escape closes. It's a modal dialog with a combobox and a listbox, and a full-screen sheet on phones.

**[ConfirmDialog](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-confirmdialog--docs)**: Asks the user to confirm an action, optionally by typing a word or name first (`alertdialog`).

**[ContextMenu](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-contextmenu--docs)**: Opens a `Menu` at the pointer when the user right-clicks inside an area, long-presses it on a touch screen, or presses Shift+F10 or the context menu key while focus is inside it (the menu then opens under the focused element, or under the item its `aria-activedescendant` points at). Pairs the area (its first child) with the `Menu` (its second child), like `MenuTrigger`. Text fields inside the area keep the browser's own menu. Keyboard and screen reader users should also reach the same actions another way, such as a "More actions" menu button.

**[Dialog](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-dialog--docs)**: A modal dialog. The page behind is dimmed and inert, focus is trapped inside and returns to the trigger on close, and the page doesn't scroll. Stacked dialogs close one at a time with Escape. On phones it's a full-screen sheet whose footer stays above the on-screen keyboard and the safe area.

**[Drawer](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-drawer--docs)**: A side sheet with the same semantics as Dialog (modal, labelled, focus trapped and returned). It slides in from the side on tablet and desktop and becomes a bottom sheet on phones. Open it from a DialogTrigger or with `isOpen`.

**[HoverCard](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-hovercard--docs)**: A card that previews what its trigger leads to (a person, a page) on hover, keyboard focus or a touch long press, after a short delay. Unlike a tooltip it may hold links and buttons; unlike a popover the trigger keeps its own action. Placed and styled like Popover, and like Popover a bottom sheet on phones. Built on React Aria's PreviewTrigger.

**[InfoTip](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-infotip--docs)**: An (i) button that opens a small popover explaining a term, by tap, click or keyboard. Unlike a tooltip it works the same with touch, and it can hold more than a word or two. On phones it opens as a bottom sheet.

**[Menu](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-menu--docs)**: A list of actions or choices with full keyboard support (arrow keys, typeahead, Escape, focus return). Inside a MenuTrigger it opens in a popover placed to avoid the screen edges, or a bottom sheet on phones; on its own it's an inline menu.

**[Menubar](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-menubar--docs)**: A desktop-app menu bar (File, Edit, View…): each of `items` is a menu, with actions, checkable items, sections, separators, submenus and shortcut hints, and choosing an item calls `onAction` with its `id`. The bar is one Tab stop; Left and Right move between the menus' names (and switch the open menu), Down, Enter or Space open one, Escape closes it, typing a name's first letters moves to it, and hovering another name while a menu is open switches to it. On phones it's one menu button, with each menu as a submenu.

**[Popover](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-popover--docs)**: A panel anchored to its trigger, with dialog semantics (focus moves in, Escape and outside clicks close it, focus returns). On phones it becomes a bottom sheet (spec phone behaviour).

**[StepDialog](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-stepdialog--docs)**: A dialog that walks through steps with per-step validation and an optional summary. Progress is a compact Stepper ("Step 2 of 4" over a segmented bar, the current segment in the danger colour while the step shows an error).

**[Tooltip](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/overlays-tooltip--docs)**: A short label for a control, typically an icon-only button. Shows on hover and keyboard focus, and briefly after a touch tap (React Aria's own tooltip never shows for touch).

## Shell

**[Brand](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/shell-brand--docs)**: The app's mark and name, linking home.

**[NotificationCenter](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/shell-notificationcenter--docs)**: A list of notifications (job finished, mention, alert) under group headings, with filter tabs, mark read, mark all read, dismiss and load more. It's a keyboard grid: arrow keys move between notifications and into a row's buttons, Enter opens one (marking it read). Unread notifications are tinted, dotted, bold and announced as unread. Usually shown by a `NotificationBell` in a drawer.

**[Page](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/shell-page--docs)**: One screen: header (title, breadcrumbs, actions, tabs) over the content.

**[Parts](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/shell-parts--docs)**: The expanded sidebar: sections with headings, badges, and a parent open around the current page.

**[Sample app](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/shell-sample-app--docs)**: A complete app frame. Resize the window (or use the viewport toolbar): phones get a drawer, a compact header and a bottom tab bar; tablets get the icon rail; desktop gets the full sidebar, which collapses to a rail. Links change the page through the app's `LinkComponent`.

## Table

**[DataTable](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/table-datatable--docs)**: A data table: sortable (client or server), paged (client, offset or cursor), selectable with a bulk-action bar (ActionBar), with row actions, row links, expandable detail and tree rows. On phones (or in narrow containers) rows become cards; on tablets low-priority columns hide and the first column stays put while the table scrolls sideways. All state can be controlled, so apps can keep it in the URL. Tree rows (`getRowChildren`, `loadRowChildren`): sorting orders each level on its own, children staying under their parent; client paging pages the top-level rows, each with its open children; selecting a group selects its children, and a group is checked when all its children are (some: indeterminate). Filter with `filterTree`.

**[EditableTable](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/table-editabletable--docs)**: A camera's six-rung exposure ladder. Tab into the grid, move with the arrow keys, press Enter (or double-click) to edit, Escape to cancel and Tab to the next cell while editing. Each exposure must be higher than the previous rung's; the row's actions move, duplicate and remove it.

**[Flowsheet](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/table-flowsheet--docs)**: Six vital signs and twelve lab values over ten times, newest first. Out-of-range values show a flag letter and a tone, critical ones a stronger tone and an icon; source flags (the hemolyzed potassium, the clumped platelets) take priority over the ranges. Tab into the grid and move with the arrow keys: each cell's tooltip gives the flag, range and note. A row header opens a trend chart. CCUX displays the flags; validating units, ranges and flags is the app's job.

**[LineItemsEditor](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/table-lineitemseditor--docs)**: An observatory shop invoice: eight lines, two tax rates and a 10% order discount. Type in a description for catalogue suggestions (choosing one fills the price); each line's actions duplicate, move and remove it. The total is announced a moment after it changes, and the editor prints as the invoice view.

**[Spreadsheet](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/table-spreadsheet--docs)**: A spreadsheet: typed columns, values parsed and checked as they're typed, pasted or filled, and the editing users expect from other spreadsheets. Click, drag, Shift+click or Shift with the arrow keys to select cells, rows (from the row numbers) or columns (from the headers); type, Enter, F2 or a double-click to edit; copy, cut and paste with the system clipboard (tab-separated, so it works with other spreadsheets); fill down (Ctrl+D) and right (Ctrl+R); Delete to clear; Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Ctrl+Y) to undo and redo. Right-click (long-press on touch, Shift+F10 on the keyboard) for the cell menu: insert, duplicate, move and delete rows, and sort, filter and column actions. Column headers have the same column actions in their menu, and can be dragged wider. Selected row numbers can be dragged to move rows. `editScope` sets what users can change: `all` (add, remove, rename, retype and reorder columns, and the data), `data` (values and rows) or `none` (read-only). Rows and columns are controlled (`onChange`, `onColumnsChange`); sorting, filters, search and hidden columns can be controlled or not. Only the rows and columns in view render, so sheets of hundreds of thousands of rows scroll smoothly.

## Terminal

**[Terminal](https://ccux.centennialoss.org/latest/?path=/docs/terminal-terminal--docs)**: A terminal (xterm.js) for a shell over the app's socket, or read-only output. Screen-reader mode is on. Tab stays in the terminal while it takes input, so a hint below it gives the way out: Ctrl+Shift+Esc moves focus to what follows it. Apps import xterm's stylesheet (`@xterm/xterm/css/xterm.css`).
